## The failure

A verification aimed at a remote host from this dev box can **succeed against
localhost** and give you a confident, precise, wrong answer.

`/etc/hosts` on this machine pins some `*.papercusp.com` names to loopback:

```
127.0.0.1 sidestage.papercusp.com media.sidestage.papercusp.com
```

So `curl https://sidestage.papercusp.com/healthz`, a `verdict goto` at that
hostname, and any browser check pointed there all hit whatever is listening
locally. Measured on this box:

```
https://sidestage.papercusp.com/  →  200, ip=127.0.0.1, 0.30s
```

**There is no tell in the response.** The local server answers with a
well-formed body — including a real-looking build sha. It matches prod only
when local happens to be serving the same build; on a stale bundle or a
branch you get a confident wrong sha with nothing in the output to catch it.

This is not hypothetical: the agent who filed the originating bug
(`EI-20732462499061834`) had already cited a sha read this way as prod
evidence in two work-items, writing "I read it off the live public /healthz."
They had not.

## Why the obvious workaround also fails

`curl --resolve <host>:443:<origin-ip>` **times out**. The office LAN drops
TLS handshakes whose SNI is `*.papercusp.com` and poisons DNS for those
names. That is *why* the release probes were moved to run on the prod host
inside the api image — see the `run_release_probe` comment in the SideStage
`deploy/deploy.sh`.

So the box has **two independent barriers** to reaching prod by hostname —
one local, one network-level — and the local one fails toward a convincing
false positive while the network one fails loudly.

A corollary worth internalising: because DNS for these names is poisoned at
the router, **a `dig @8.8.8.8` answer for `*.papercusp.com` is not
trustworthy either.** Do not treat any IP you resolve here as "the real
origin".

## What protects you now

`apps/operator/scripts/hooks/cc/guard-operator-desktop.mjs` (PreToolUse)
blocks browser-navigation MCP tools and the `verdict` skill when the target
hostname **looks remote but resolves to loopback**. The block names the host
and prints `getent hosts <host>` so you can confirm the pin yourself.

Deliberate scope limits, so you know what it does *not* cover:

- **Explicitly-local targets stay allowed.** `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`,
  `*.local` — pointing there is an intentional local check, not a deception.
- **A split-horizon name stays allowed.** Only an *all-loopback* answer
  guarantees the connection lands locally.
- **It fails OPEN** on any resolver error, missing `getent`, or unparseable
  payload. A guard that blocks on its own resolver failure is worse than the
  bug it prevents.
- **`curl` in Bash is NOT intercepted.** The hook deliberately does not match
  Bash (a text-scanning matcher false-positives on anything that merely
  mentions a hostname). A shell `curl` at a pinned host is still on you.

## What to do instead

In descending order of trust:

1. **Run the probe on the prod host**, as `deploy.sh` does —
   `docker run --rm --network host … --entrypoint node <image> /probe/<script> --base-url https://<host>`.
2. **`ssh` to the host + container-exec the healthz** — prod's own process
   answering for itself.
3. **Verify against localhost deliberately** — legitimate for UI behaviour,
   *provided the evidence says "localhost"*. The dishonesty is not checking
   localhost; it is checking localhost and writing "prod".

## Do not "fix" this by deleting the hosts entry

The pin may be load-bearing. The line immediately above it
(`flags.papercuspai.com`) is a documented, owner-gated workaround for
router-level DNS poisoning, deliberately chosen so it fails *fast* rather
than hanging. Removing a pin reflexively can trade a loud failure for a hang.
**The fix is detection at the verification seam, which is now in place.**

## Repro

```bash
getent hosts sidestage.papercusp.com                      # → 127.0.0.1 (the whole bug)
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{remote_ip}\n' \
     https://sidestage.papercusp.com/                     # → 200 127.0.0.1
curl -s --max-time 15 --resolve sidestage.papercusp.com:443:<origin> \
     https://sidestage.papercusp.com/                     # → exit 28, timeout
```
